theorem_title: Cyclic deficit nonnegative on norm-capped group 0
formal_statement:
theorem HlawkaSchatten.DiagonalCutoff21.domain_nonneg_group00 :
    ∀ p : ℝ, (21 : ℝ) ≤ p → p ≤ (377/16 : ℝ) → ∀ X : Fin 3 → Fin 3 → ℝ,
      (∀ j, -(5559/5000 : ℝ) ≤ X j j ∧ X j j ≤ -(881/2000 : ℝ)) →
      (∀ j i, j ≠ i → (3779/5000 : ℝ) ≤ X j i ∧ X j i ≤ (11847/10000 : ℝ)) →
      (∀ j, lpNorm p (X j) ≤ (1193402307/1000000000 : ℝ)) →
      lpNorm p (X 0 + X 1 + X 2) ≤ (3033/2500 : ℝ) →
      (∀ i j k : Fin 3, i ≠ j → i ≠ k → j ≠ k → (1139124440087/716625000000 : ℝ) ≤ X j i + X k i) →
      (3314799982801/573300000000 : ℝ) ≤ X 0 1 + X 0 2 + X 1 0 + X 1 2 + X 2 0 + X 2 1 →
      0 ≤ tripleDeficit p (cyclicConstant p) X := by sorry
preamble:
import Definitions.Def_HlawkaSchatten_GapComparison
import Definitions.Def_HlawkaSchatten_DiagonalConstruction_Basic
import Definitions.Def_HlawkaSchatten_DiagonalConstruction_NormHessian
import Definitions.Def_HlawkaSchatten_DiagonalConstruction_BoxGeometry
import Definitions.Def_HlawkaSchatten_DiagonalConstruction_BoxCoordinates
import Definitions.Def_HlawkaSchatten_DiagonalConstruction_BoxConvexity
import Definitions.Def_HlawkaSchatten_DiagonalConstruction_BoxHessian
import Definitions.Def_HlawkaSchatten_DiagonalConstruction_Cyclic
import Definitions.Def_HlawkaSchatten_DiagonalConstruction_Normalization
open HlawkaSchatten HlawkaSchatten.DiagonalConstruction
natural_language_statement: For every real p in [21,377/16], a real three-coordinate triple satisfying the displayed diagonal and off-diagonal coordinate intervals, actual singleton norm caps, actual total norm cap, linear complementary-pair coordinate floors and linear off-diagonal-sum floor has nonnegative original Hlawka deficit for the unchanged cyclic constant. No equality of singleton norms is assumed. Pointwise seven-norm Hessian estimates imply convexity on this invariant domain, and permutation averaging reduces the assertion to the defining cyclic supremum.
source: Yuxuan Xu, A computer-assisted sharp diagonal Hlawka inequality for real exponents p >= 21, Sections 5-7, https://github.com/Anchen-AI4Math/hlawka-diagonal-certificates/blob/main/paper/main.pdf . Generic norm/averaging framework by Ezzeri Esa, Apache-2.0; original notices retained.
explanation: All generic norm-Hessian, coefficient, radial-spread, six-pair matrix, domain convexity, line derivative and permutation averaging proofs are embedded. Exact rational grouped geometry and real-exponent numeric margins prove Hessian nonnegativity. The two already Proved original scalar milestones fix the actual cyclicConstant coefficient. This extracts the shared analytic theorem, so finite contraction certificates can import it without recompiling the full analytic argument.
